institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Aspects include course opportunities, language, nature experiences, and the country's culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The assistance was great, and you were provided with all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some information meetings during the intro week, some info flyers, and detailed emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Relatively easy. It can be recommended to use Norwiegen's own sites, especially
Hybel.no
.
NOT
Finn.no
(here it was difficult to find only for one semester).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is perfectly fine, many do it because the whole city is a "student city". Also you get the change to live with local people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find housing through the university, so recommend trying to find something private.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration seemed complicated at first since you have a lot of information to keep track of. But NTNU's own platform made it easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different contact mails/people, if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me easy, but it was luck that since many had trouble switching around so their schedules and exams would not overlap. On the bright side, there were a lot of time to decide, so you could try out different classes before deciding.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have a good time deciding, so don't stress.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The BA levels were perhaps a bit lower than expected but might be due to the fact that it was introduction courses. The MA level was harder than expected, but very giving.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were pretty much the same style. However, I experienced a lot fewer lecture-exercises, which is very common at KU and a nice way to work with the learning material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1. Introduction to Neuroscience (15 ECTS). 2. Immunology (7.5 ECTS). 3. Intorduction to molecular medicine (7.5 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Neuroscience. This course was very big, but all lectures were online, making it very flexible (at the same time, the downside of the course), and the exam was easy to get through. Otherwise, Immunology was probably my favorite course with a supporting exercise classes and just overall interesting subjects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cost to nice outdoor clothes and shoes.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer and alcohol were pretty expensive. Fish and mushrooms was less expensive than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of social activities through Studentersamfundet, NTNUi (idræt), and ESN with opportunities both for nice trips in Norway, different sports clubs, or just social groups for almost everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A trip to Lofoten, either arranged privately or through ESN. Also, visit a koi through NTNUi which has small cabins you can visit.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again, visit Lofoten. Enjoy the city. Go on a hike in Bymarka or other places where you can find a small cabin to eat waffles.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, since the culture is vary like one in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was a challenge that people were so bad at taking the bus without blocking the whole bus and not making room for other people (when there were a lot of free space).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love for nature and active lifestyle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Bring good footwear, you will not regret it. 
2. Remember to enjoy and travel the country.
3. Try to get a room and live with Norwegians. Otherwise, you won't get in contact with them that easy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The overall experience. The people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: If it gets icy on the street.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
